description:
Bug (reproduced 2026-11-09 on 8b6bcf01f): the collector misreads live objects as forwarded. is_forwarded_headerless (runtime/src/heap/gc/forwarding.rs) treats "word0 low nibble == 0x8 and word1 == 0x8 exactly" as forwarded. A live bitstring has word0 = bit_len and word1 = its first 8 bytes, so <<8,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,1>> (72 bits = 0x48) is read as forwarded to 0x40. JIT run: SIGSEGV, exit 139. The same program with first byte 7 runs 19 collections and prints the binary. Probe: keep b = make(8) where make(x) = <<x,0,0,0,0,0,0,0,1>> live across churn(20000, []) (list of Integer.to_string), then dbg(b). A struct whose schema_id ends in 8 (from 24 up) with first field raw 8 has the same exposure (unprobed; the builder probes it). The check dates from fz-3ld (#41).

Design (user, 2026-11-09): every heap pointer is 16-byte aligned, so its low nibble is 0000. Make the forwarding marker the SOLE use of the low bits: the marker lives in a word whose live value has a zero low nibble by construction, and "low nibble != 0" means forwarded. One read, no confirm word, no false positives.

Per kind:
- ProcBin / Resource: word 0 is a 16-aligned pointer; already a one-word check.
- List cons: put the marker in word 1, the link (16-aligned tail address; head kind and alias bits are high). The head word is left alone.
- Struct, Closure, Map, Bitstring: word 0 is a header (schema id + flags, denotation + closure header, map header with MAP_DESTINATION_FLAG at bit 63, bit length). Give each header a layout whose low nibble is zero (e.g. numeric fields kept above bit 4). Codegen reads/writes some headers directly (static struct literals in native_codegen/prim.rs write schema_id at bytes 0..4; check every reader/writer in runtime, JIT, AOT and the interpreter).

Fold in the low-bit kind encoding: refs already carry kind in the high bits, fields store raw address + side-band kind byte, list links carry kind high. The remaining low-tag currency (heap_kind_from_tagged, decode_tagged_heap_bits, tagged "strict bits" in gc/forward.rs and deep_copy.rs, object_size's tag match, MSO chain links' kind in low bits in procbin.rs, the TAG_MASK checks in ir_runtime.rs and ir_interp/value.rs) moves to the high-bit / side-band forms. TAG_FWD stops being a member of the kind space.

Done when:
- The crash probe and a struct-header probe are fixtures (fz-a9y/gl6 block, next free number) that pass on interp, run and build; the bitstring one fails on the parent.
- Forwarding detection is one read of one word per kind; copy_to_space_with_confirmed_forwarding's confirm write and is_forwarded_headerless's confirm read are gone.
- No production code tests a pointer's or a value's low nibble except the forwarding-marker predicate (grep TAG_MASK proves it); TAG_FWD is not a ValueKind tag.
- A heap unit test per kind: a live object whose payload imitates the old marker pattern survives a collection unchanged.
- No fixture pin changes (header layout must not change object sizes); report any that move with the mechanism.
- Documentation in the same commit: every .agent/docs page, guide (guides/*.html), README.md section and fixture README that describes a mechanism this ticket changes or removes is rewritten to the present fact in the same commit, and a grep for the old names and phrases over .agent, guides, README.md and fixtures returns nothing. Full gate green (--workspace --all-targets plus doc tests, fixture matrix with --test-threads=1). Commit in Why / What changed / Verification form. No co-author trailer, no attribution line.
title: The low nibble belongs only to the forwarding marker
